# Chapter Nineteen: The Truth of the Genome

The library smelled of woodsmoke, old leather, and the pungent, earthy aroma of Rebecca's crushed herbal poultice.

Father Edgar lay propped up on the large leather sofa, his head wrapped in clean linen bandages, a cup of hot tea laced with medicinal whisky resting in his trembling hand. Rebecca worked with surgical efficiency, her fingers glowing with a faint, warm amber luminescence as she massaged a thick salve of comfrey, silver-leaf, and mountain arnica into the priest's bruised ribs. Under her touch, the swelling receded at a rate that defied modern medical science.

"You've got gentle hands for a wolf, lass," Edgar muttered, wincing as she set a dislocated finger with a sharp click. "My grandmother in Inverness used to make a brew like that for sprained ankles, but it never smelled this foul."

"Your grandmother wasn't treating a man who got hit by an eight-hundred-pound Lycan," Rebecca replied with a faint, wry smile. "Rest, Father. The internal bleeding has stopped. Your ribs will be fully knit by dawn."

Across the refectory table, Victor sat opposite Alfonso. *Lobera* lay unseathed between them, resting on a woolen blanket, its celestial steel gleaming in the firelight. Beside it, the Jamestown dagger caught the reflection of the flames.

Victor rubbed his temples, staring intently at the ancient Alpha. "In the visions... when I held the dagger... I lived your memories, Alfonso. I felt your fear outside the Jamestown settlement. I felt your uncle hitting your shoulders, telling you to keep the blade up. How is that possible? How can a piece of iron store a man's thoughts?"

Alfonso reached out, his weathered finger hovering just above the gold lettering on the blade without touching it. "It isn't ordinary iron, Victor. In the summer of 1217, an enormous bolide—a meteorite from deep space—fell in the Sierra Morena mountains north of Cordoba. King Ferdinand's royal metallurgists extracted sixty pounds of celestial iron from the crater. The metal possessed an extraordinary molecular crystalline matrix that reacted directly to human bio-electric frequencies."

"A biological conductor," Victor realized softly.

"Exactly," Alfonso said. "When Ferdinand had Lobera and its companion daggers forged in Toledo, they were tempered in oils infused with his own blood. The steel became a living genealogical record. Only those who carry the direct genetic sequence of Castile can awaken its frequency. When you held the dagger in Rockville, the crystalline matrix recognized your DNA and discharged the residual neuro-synaptic impressions I left behind three centuries ago."

Victor leaned forward, his voice dropping. "And the wolves? Bishop Talbot told me they were demons. He said Lucifer cursed human bloodlines during the Crusades to create predators of the night."

Alfonso let out a low, weary chuckle, shaking his head. "The Church has always excelled at turning biology into demonology whenever it suited their territorial ambitions. The Lycanthrope genome is not a curse, Victor. It is an ancient Pleistocene adaptation. Over forty thousand years ago, during the deepest freeze of the Wurm glaciation, early human tribes faced extinction. A small percentage of the Cro-Magnon population underwent an evolutionary divergence—a genetic mutation that allowed human cells to rapidly hyper-metabolize, altering bone density, muscle fiber, and sensory organs into an apex predatory form."

Rebecca paused in her work, looking over from the sofa. "We were humanity's guardians, Victor. When prehistoric predators and rival human clans sought to wipe out early settlements, the Lycan clans defended the perimeter. For twenty thousand years, man and wolf walked together in sacred balance."

"Then what happened?" Victor asked.

"Civilization happened," Alfonso answered grimly. "As men congregated in walled cities, they forgot the wilderness. They began to fear what they could no longer control. In the Middle Ages, the rising power of the feudal Church saw the Lycan clans not as guardians, but as an existential threat to their ecclesiastical authority. If a village was protected by a wolf clan, why would they pay tithes to the bishop for holy protection? So the Inquisition was born. The guardians were labeled monsters, and the holy hunts began."

Alfonso gestured toward *Lobera*. "King Ferdinand III was the first ruler to understand this. He forged Lobera not to exterminate the wolves, but to police the boundary. Lobera was designed as an Arbiter's weapon—powerful enough to execute rogue beasts who preyed on humans, but balanced by the royal oath to protect peaceful packs from extermination. Ferdinand established the First Covenant. But after his death, corrupt inquisitors poisoned his successors, suppressed the truth, and turned the Order of Saint Francis into an engine of genocide."

A sudden, ragged cough came from the sofa. Edgar pushed himself upright, his face pale, his eyes burning with urgency.

"Alfonso speaks the truth, Victor," Edgar wheezed, clutching his chest. "And God forgive me, but I didn't realize how far the rot had spread until tonight. Captain Mercer... he didn't come to Scotland to support your training, lad. Mercer heads the Custodes Sanguinis. He has spent the last five years developing a weaponized bio-silver compound called Argentum-9."

Rebecca's head snapped up, her amber eyes flaring with primal terror. "Argentum-9? The aerosol micro-silver?"

"Aye, lass," Edgar said grimly. "A pressurized dispersal system mounted on a heavy military transport. Mercer has staged the rig at the ruins of Saint Jude's Monastery in Glen Clova. The valley is home to Fiona's highland pack—thirty wolf families, including elders and nursing cubs. Brock fled there because he thinks he can bargain with Mercer for safe passage back to America. But Mercer doesn't bargain. He intends to trigger the aerosol payload at sunrise."

"What will the gas do?" Victor asked, his stomach turning.

"To mortal lungs, it causes mild irritation," Edgar said, his voice trembling with shame. "But to anyone carrying the active Lycan genome, it causes acute, systemic pulmonary necrosis. Their lungs will dissolve in their chests within two minutes. The entire valley will become a mass grave."

Alfonso stood up, his jaw set like carved granite, his towering frame casting a long shadow across the hearth. "Glen Clova is surrounded by steep granite ridges. If Mercer releases the aerosol into the valley mist, the gas will sink into the lowlands. Not a single wolf will survive."

Victor looked down at *Lobera*. The celestial iron gleamed in the firelight, reflecting the determination in his eyes. He thought of Jessica and his children, sleeping peacefully in the protective safe house three thousand miles away. He had agreed to take up this blade to protect his family from being hunted.

Now he understood that true protection did not come from slaughtering innocents in the dark; it came from standing between the butcher and the prey.

Victor reached out, took the grip of *Lobera*, and slid it into the leather scabbard across his back. He picked up the Jamestown dagger and latched it to his belt.

"How far is Glen Clova?" Victor asked, his voice steady, commanding, and clear.

Marcus grabbed his tactical bag from the floor. "Forty-five minutes through the mountain passes."

"Then we move now," Victor said, looking Alfonso dead in the eye. "The First Covenant was broken seven hundred years ago. Tonight, we forge the New one."

---
